sampling_model.design: An i.i.d. observational sample augmented by deterministic public nuisance functions \((m_0,m_1,p)\), supplied global \(L^2(P_X)\) error radii bounded by the fixed cap \(\bar r\), a fixed signal envelope \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\leq M\), and decision rules that may use all public inputs.
sampling_model.units: Independent units \(O_i=(Y_i,D_i,X_i)\), \(i=1,\ldots,n\), from a causal law satisfying consistency and conditional ignorability.
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with propensity \(e(X)\), positive almost surely and allowed to approach zero.
sampling_model.overlap: Uniform one-sided dyadic shells satisfy \(c_-u^{\kappa}\leq P\{u/2<e(X)\leq u\}\leq c_+u^{\kappa}\) for \(0<u\leq\lambda_0\), while \(e(X)\leq1-\eta_+\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: The minimax infima range over rules measurable in \(O^{(n)}\) that also receive \(m_0\), \(m_1\), \(p\), \(r_{0n}\), \(r_{1n}\), and \(r_{en}\). The same public inputs are fixed within each lower family, the certified radii lie in \([0,\bar r]\), and each fuzzy family uses finite equal-cell refinements of a complete countable reservoir with signal--balancing pairs.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives a squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bound in the paper's estimator-bounded class; for constant weight, the interpretive squared-radius mapping yields \(n^{-1/2}+\max\{r_{0n},r_{1n}\}r_{en}\), while Remark 2 retains the treated-side lower-bound form with known baseline response.

Section 2 gives the lower-rate form \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\) for one mean functional in its pure structure-agnostic class; the attested passage supplies neither a control-arm extension, a joint two-arm ATE equivalence, nor a matching upper bound for this note's comparator class.
Thresholded AIPW is uniformly asymptotically normal under sufficient weak-overlap nuisance conditions.
IPW has Gaussian or stable limits according to tail and trimming regimes.
Extreme propensity scores generate non-Gaussian limit theory for IPW and doubly robust estimators.
Localized fuzzy hypotheses yield a minimax lower bound for pointwise CATE.
Inverse-weight estimation can have tail-dependent irregular rates.
Limited-overlap confidence accuracy is driven by local comparison-cell sizes.
Section 6.1 treats bounded-overlap ATE examples, while the conclusion identifies weak-overlap distribution shift as an open extension.

Theorem 3.1 gives asymptotic linearity and a studentized Gaussian limit for bias-corrected trimmed doubly robust estimators targeting the original treatment-effect estimand, with Proposition B.1 verifying the ATE specialization.

body.tldr: For fixed one-sided dyadic-shell constants satisfying both \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\), the absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability for each fixed \(\delta\in(0,\delta_0]\), and honest expected-length for each fixed \(\alpha\in(0,1/4)\) frontiers all equal the four-channel rate \(\rho_n\) up to constants.  The clipped estimator, five-block median, and interval upper bounds hold on the broader uniform one-sided-shell class with those two richness conditions deleted.  An exported all-\(N\) inequality gives \(E_P|\widehat\tau_{\lambda,N}-\tau(P)|\leq C_{\mathrm{FT}}U_N(\lambda)\), the explicit oracle comparison gives \(U_n(\lambda_n^\star)\leq C_{\mathrm{opt}}\rho_n\), and \(C_\star=C_{\mathrm{FT}}C_{\mathrm{opt}}\) yields the computable interval multiplier \(K_\alpha=C_\star\max\{\sqrt{10}(10/\alpha)^{1/3},\alpha^{-1}\}\).  Adaptation to unknown shell and nuisance certificates remains open.

project_justification.gap: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR supplies WATE lower-bound templates in its estimator-bounded source class, whereas BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE supplies a lower-rate statement for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class.  Neither published class is nested with the present dyadic-shell public-function experiment, so neither citation supports class inclusion or a transferred minimax theorem.  Weak-overlap papers give trimming rules, irregular limits, or sufficient Wald conditions rather than this finite-sample four-risk frontier with an evaluable honest interval.
project_justification.niche: The public-function model isolates the statistical price of knowing only global prediction-error guarantees when treated observations vanish at a boundary.  Its all-\(N\), all-threshold bound keeps the public certificates indexed by the original experiment, so the same inequality controls the full sample and every median block.  Upper estimation and coverage require only the uniform one-sided-shell law; the matching converse requires both explicit reservoir-richness inequalities.
project_justification.fill: The paper supplies the clipped estimator, five-block median, and a bias-aware interval with the closed-form constants \(C_{\mathrm{FT}}\), \(C_{\mathrm{opt}}\), \(C_\star\), and \(K_\alpha\).  On the broader shell class these objects attain the four-channel upper rate.  On the reservoir-rich subclass, the established signal-only four-channel construction supplies matching absolute-risk, root-MSE, fixed-probability, and honest expected-length lower bounds.

body.related_work: JinSyrgkanis2024StructureAgnosticDR, Theorem 1 and Remark 2, gives squared quantile-minimax WATE lower bounds in its estimator-bounded source class. BonviniKennedyDukesBalakrishnan2024StructureAgnosticATE, Section 2, gives the lower-rate form \(n^{-1/2}+\varepsilon_n\delta_n\) for one mean functional in a different uniformly overlapped structure-agnostic source class; the attested statement supplies neither a control-arm extension nor a joint two-arm ATE equivalence. Neither published class is nested with this note's dyadic-shell public-function experiment. Accordingly, the fast-tail calculation in \(\texttt{prop:regular-benchmark-reduction}\) is only an algebraic, source-scoped sanity comparison and proves no class inclusion, transferred lower bound, or transferred minimax equivalence. Dorn2025WeakOverlapTStatistics, MaSantAnnaSasakiUra2026DRWeakOverlap, MaWang2020RobustIPW, and HeilerKazak2021ExtremePropensity study Gaussian or non-Gaussian inference, trimming, or threshold selection rather than this matched public-function minimax frontier. KennedyBalakrishnanRobinsWasserman2024MinimaxCATE supplies a fuzzy-hypothesis template for a different estimand and smoothness class; KhanTamer2010Irregular explains the tail-driven inverse-weight obstruction; Rothe2017RobustCI studies limited-overlap coverage under finite-cell or auxiliary structure. The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp papers likewise concern non-nested targets and law classes.
body.interpretation: The regular-benchmark reduction is only an algebraic check: as \(\kappa\to\infty\), the treated side has the same parametric-plus-product form as the verified published lower-bound templates after their explicit radius identifications. Bonvini's attested one-functional statement is used only for the treated-side mapping \(\varepsilon_n=r_{1n}\), \(\delta_n=r_{en}\); no control-arm term is attributed to that source. The shell class and the regular comparator class are disjoint, so the calculation establishes neither minimax equivalence nor inclusion transfer. The accepted policy-regret and continuous-exposure clamp frontiers answer non-nested causal decision problems under non-nested law classes.
body.technical_internal_limitation: The converse uses reservoir-rich fixed shell constants satisfying \(\texttt{ass:lower-shell-richness}\) and \(\texttt{ass:upper-shell-richness}\). Its probability law is complete: the displayed background mass is less than one half, active signal and balancing masses total \(2As_0^\kappa\), explicit completion masses sum to the remaining mass, and all three pieces sum exactly to one. Every active mass is relocated from a virtual dyadic endpoint into a fixed interior fraction of its shell; the relocation cap proves the upper shell inequality even when nonemptiness leaves no unused global capacity. Treated fuzzy propensities have ratios in \([4/5,4/3]\), control fuzzy propensities in \([3/4,5/4]\), and opposite-tilt companions make each fixed-sign propensity multiset invariant. At \(\kappa=1\), the proof uses exact dyadic sums for \(\lVert f\rVert_2^2\), \(E[e_0f^2]\), and \(E[f]\), not density or integral heuristics. The upper bound needs no reservoir richness, so shell classes outside the stated richness regime may have different converse geometry.
body.honest_scope: The theorem concerns supplied public functions, bounded certified radii, fixed shell constants, and \(E_P[(g_1(X)-g_0(X))^2]\leq M\); it imposes no pointwise potential-outcome envelope and makes no Wald or Gaussian-limit claim.  The confidence interval is bias-aware and is evaluable when the oracle certificates and fixed class constants are supplied: its multiplier is the displayed algebraic \(K_\alpha\).  The upper interval needs no reservoir richness, whereas matching length optimality uses both richness assumptions.  Adaptation to unknown shell constants, tail exponent, and nuisance radii, bounded-outcome variants, shell constants outside the richness regime, and exact studentized validity remain open.
